newsitem.title: FRANCE: TENNIS-KUERTEN LEADS BRUGUERA 6-3 IN FRENCH OPEN FINAL.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-KUERTEN LEADS BRUGUERA 6-3 IN FRENCH OPEN FINAL.

text.p: Unseeded Gustavo Kuerten of Brazil led 16th seed Sergi Bruguera of Spain 6-3 in the French Open men's singles final on Sunday:

Gustavo Kuerten seemed to have an early edge, winning his first two service games to love while Bruguera was struggling to hold his. Playing well inside the court, the 20-year-old Brazilian upset the Spaniard's baseline game and broke him at the net to lead 3-2.
Dictating the pace thanks to his powerful forehands and fast backhands, Kuerten easily took the upper hand and broke Bruguera again in the ninth game to take the first set in 28 minutes.

On a high, Kuerten again won his first service game to love to lead 1-0. He then earned a break point at the end of an unbelievable rally in which the talented Brazilian showed a huge variety of shots against the 1993 and 1994 champion.
Bruguera, a true fighter, survived this extraordinary display of attacking tennis but bowed two games later, despite a brave attempt to change tactics and rush the net.
Kuerten showed a first sign of weariness in the following game, in which a couple of unforced errors allowed Bruguera to break back to trail 3-2.
Momentum seemed to be changing when the Spaniard twice passed the young Brazilian to obtain three break points in the ninth game but Kuerten fought back and held his serve for 5-4.
The Brazilian finally broke the deadlock in the following game and won the set 6-4 on his second set point.
Aware that a straight-set defeat was looming, Bruguera gave it all he had to try and break Kuerten in the beginning of the third set.
A little less consistent than in the first two sets, the young Bralizian still had enough strength left to fight back from 15-40 and 30-40 down on his first two service games and lead 2-1.
Now there was no stopping Kuerten, who earned another break point on a drop shot in the seventh game and broke for 4-2 when Bruguera hit a forehand long.
Exhausted, Bruguera was unable to take another game. A volley into the net made Kuerten the first Brazilian to win a Grand Slam tournament.
